label: <DEL> step of long sequences, content-gated (first token x/m/s/p/1/t)
explanation: Fires mainly on the <DEL> step (80% of activation mass, 73% of active steps), but only on about 9% of delimiter steps. Rate rises steeply with L: 2x lift at L=7, about 5x at t=8-9, and L=9 carries 52% of the mass. Which delimiter steps it fires on depends on sequence content: first token (and the first output) x, m, s, p, 1 or t gives about 3-5x lift. The other 20% of mass is on late original-phase steps (t >= 7, mostly first occurrences of a token, often 3, c or e) just before <DEL>, so it often ramps up over the last few inputs. Essentially silent at t <= 1, in the copy phase (15 steps), and on repeated tokens. Content gating looks distributed (top examples are rich in d, i, k, j), and no simple token-set predicate captures it; the best predicate reaches dev F1 0.43 and mass recall 0.51.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: x, m, p, s, 1, t; least: j, 3, e, b) and the next token to output (most: s, m, x, i, p, d; least: e, b, j, 3); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, t=8, t=3.
